articles.title: Rafa Jódar cae en segunda ronda de Basilea y deja su condición de 'top10' en manos de Djokovic
articles.standfirst: El madrileño pierde con Vacherot y Nole y De Miñaur le pasarán en el ranking si alcanzan las semifinales
articles.summary: El madrileño pierde con Vacherot y Nole y De Miñaur le pasarán en el ranking si alcanzan las semifinales
articles.body: Rafa Jódar, en su primera temporada entre los mayores, jugaba en Basilea con un triple objetivo: ganar el segundo título como profesional, estrenarse como 'top10' mundial y afianzarse en las posiciones que dan billete para las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). No podrá lograr seguro dos de las tres metas. Y estar entre los 10 mejores queda en manos de Novak Djokovic tras su derrota este jueves en la segunda ronda a manos de Valentin Vacherot, por 7-6(4), 2-6 y 7-6(5), en 2 horas y 30 minutos. Si Djokovic alcanza las semifinales en tierras suizas y Alex de Miñaur hace lo propio en Viena retrasarán el estreno de Rafa entre los 10 mejores del planeta. El serbio, el australiano (a 29 puntos del español) y Taylor Fritz son sus tres rivales directos en el ranking. Y los tres siguen con vida esta semana: De Miñaur es cuartofinalista de Viena y Nole y Fritz están clasificados para la segunda ronda de Basilea. Todos están en la puja por lograr uno de los cinco billetes restantes de la cita de maestros. Todo estará en juego del 2 al 8 de noviembre en el Masters 1000 de París. Allí habrá una bolsa de 1.000 puntos al campeón. El balance anual de Jódar es de 57 partidos ganados de los 76 disputados. Sólo Alexander Zverev, número 1 virtual, ganó más que él este curso. Jódar se quedó a tan sólo dos puntos de firmar la quinta remontada en los últimos ocho partidos. El joven de Leganés dispuso de dos servicios, con 5-4 en la muerte súbita de la tercera manga. Perdió los dos puntos con el saque y esa fue su condena.

articles.title: A qué hora es el Alcaraz - Paul: horario y dónde ver en TV y online los cuartos del torneo de Viena
articles.standfirst: Será el décimo enfrentamiento entre ambos y el murciano domina por siete victorias a dos
articles.summary: Será el décimo enfrentamiento entre ambos y el murciano domina por siete victorias a dos
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ya está en los cuartos de final del Open 500 de Viena tras pasar por encima del georgiano Nikoloz Basilashvili. En la siguiente ronda espera Tommy Paul, el decimocuarto de las listas a sus 29 años y que ya sabe lo que es ganar al español. Lo hizo en dos de los nueve enfrentamientos entre ambos. Carlitos, sin embargo, se ha apuntado los seis últimos precedentes. Para encontrar el triunfo más reciente del americano hay que remontarse a los cuartos del Masters 1000 de Canadá, en 2023. Paul se ganó el pase a la antepenúltima ronda de Viena tras superar con suficiencia al italiano Luciano Darderi, por un doble 6-1. El estadounidense es decimotercero en la Race 2016, con 2.725 puntos, y conserva opciones matemáticas de hacerse con una de las cinco plazas restantes para estar en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). El partido de cuartos de final de Viena entre Carlos Alcaraz y Nikoloz Basilashvili se disputará este viernes 30 de octubre, en la central del Marx Halle de la capital austriaca, en el segundo turno del día, sobre las 15:30 horas. Los cuartos de final del torneo de Viena entre Carlos Alcaraz y Nikoloz Basilashvili se podrán seguir a través de de Movistar +, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Tennis: Alexander Zverev to replace Jannik Sinner as ATP world number one after beating Tallon Girekspoor in Vienna
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner as men’s world number one at his earliest opportunity after reaching the Vienna quarter-finals.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner as the men’s world number one at his earliest opportunity after reaching the quarter-finals in Vienna.

He was already guaranteed to finish 2026 as the ATP’s leading player, but made sure he will rise to the summit on Monday with a 6-4 7-5 win over Tallon Griekspoor at the Erste Bank Open.

Zverev, 29, is the second German to reach the pinnacle of the men's tour after Boris Becker in 1991.

The achievement is a testament to his body of work this year, having won two Grand Slam titles and 64 of his 80 matches.

"It's been a wait but sometimes you have to wait for the best things in life," said Zverev, who is the second oldest man to top the rankings for the first time.

"I'm super happy, super thrilled - I have no words for this year."

At the start of the year it seemed unthinkable that anybody other than Sinner or Carlos Alcaraz would become world number one.

But the dominant duo have missed large chunks of this season through injury, opening the door for Zverev - who won the French Open and US Open titles with at least one of the pair absent - to take over.

Going into 2026, Alcaraz led the rankings with 12,050 points, closely followed by Sinner on 11,500.

The pair's duopoly - splitting all of the eight Grand Slam titles in 2024 and 2025 between them - was illustrated by the huge gap to the rest of the field.

Third-ranked Zverev had 5,110 points - closer numerically to the 2,221st player in the world than the top two.

Both his major triumphs came without having to face Sinner or Alcaraz, and he did not face a top-10 player until beating Ben Shelton in the New York final.

As the season entered its final stretch, Zverev achieved what many thought was impossible by securing the year-end number one ranking when Alcaraz lost in Shanghai on 12 October.

Zverev knew he still could not overtake Sinner until 2 November at the earliest, but beat Griekspoor to become the first man other than Sinner and Alcaraz to top the rankings since Novak Djokovic in June 2024.

Zverev conceded he would "maybe not" be the world's best player if both his rivals were "healthy and at the top of their game".

But he has efficiently beaten what has been in front of him, recording the greatest season of a career which had threatened to fall short of the lofty expectations placed on him since emerging as a teenage prodigy.

Fery continues to prove himself - and faces Zverev next

Zverev goes on to face British number one Arthur Fery in the quarter-finals - a repeat of their Wimbledon semi-final.

Fery, 24, made an unexpected run to the SW19 last four in July, but continued to prove he belongs among the world's best with a 6-4 5-7 6-4 win over Italy's Lorenzo Musetti in Vienna.

Trailing 4-2 in the decider, Fery showed his mental fortitude by breaking straight back and then overcoming what seemed to be cramp to serve out an impressive victory.

It is easy to forget Fery is still inexperienced at the elite level following his Wimbledon heroics.

Beating former world number five Musetti - now ranked 26th after injury - represents his biggest win by ranking on the regular ATP Tour and provides another opportunity to test himself against the very best.

Fery returns to Grand Slam stage - what lies ahead?

However, Cameron Norrie fell short of his best victory of the season when world number five Daniil Medvedev saved match point to win their last-16 match.

A frustrating year has seen Norrie drop to 41st in the world rankings and exit each of the past three Grand Slam tournaments in the first round.

But the 31-year-old showed his key attributes - tenacity, athleticism and controlled aggression - to threaten a huge upset against Medvedev.

Third seed Medvedev, fresh from winning the Almaty title last week, was left angrily punching the surface when he fell a break down in the deciding set.

Norrie served for the match at 5-3 40-30, but Medvedev picked off his opponent's serve-volley attempt and fought back to win 4-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1).

Second seed Alcaraz also progressed with a 6-1 7-6 (13-11) win over Georgia's Nikoloz Basilashvili.

Meanwhile, Novak Djokovic's hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals were harmed by a second-round defeat at the Swiss Indoors event in Basel.

The 24-time major champion, 39, lost 7-6 (7-4) 5-7 6-7 (5-7) to Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff, who produced some inspired tennis to beat the Serb for the first time in nine attempts.

articles.title: Cobolli se derrumba tras lesionarse en Viena y Berrettini pasa a cuartos
articles.standfirst: Flavio se está jugando su presencia en las ATP Finals y la fase final de la Copa Davis donde iba a ser el número 1 de Italia
articles.summary: Flavio se está jugando su presencia en las ATP Finals y la fase final de la Copa Davis donde iba a ser el número 1 de Italia
articles.body: Flavio Cobolli, flamante finalista de Roland Garros y número seis del ranking ATP, se ha derrumbado este jueves en la segunda ronda de Viena que le enfrentaba a su compatriota Matteo Berrettini. Con 5-2 abajo, el italiano ha decidido abandonar entre lágrimas al recaer de sus problemas en la pierna que ya arrastraba desde el torneo de Lyon. Se ha sentado en la silla de cambios y ha tenido que ser Matteo el que acudiera a consolarle. Tenía razones Cobolli para llorar porque está en peligro lo que resta de temporada. En el horizonte el Masters 1000 de París, como antesala de las ATP Finals de Turín y la fase final de la Copa Davis donde iba ser el número 1 del equipo transalpino defensor de la corona. Berrettini, que no aparece en la convocatoria de Italia para la Copa Davis de Bolonia, podría ser repescado por el capitán Filippo Volandri si Cobolli finalmente causa baja por lesión.

images.caption: Cobolli, consolado por Berrettini.

articles.title: Djokovic se la pega ante Struff en Basilea y relanza las opciones de Jódar para ser 'top10' y estar en Turín
articles.standfirst: El alemán, enorme al servicio, gana por primera vez al serbio tras ocho derrotas
articles.summary: El alemán, enorme al servicio, gana por primera vez al serbio tras ocho derrotas
articles.body: Novak Djokovic, que parecía ser la gran amenaza de Rafa Jódar para el 'top10' y las ATP Finals de Turín ha quedado eliminado por sorpresa este jueves en la segunda ronda de Basilea. Su verdugo ha sido Jan-Lennard Struff, un rival que había claudicado en los ocho precedentes entre ambos. El gigante alemán cerró un marcador favorable de 6-7(4), 7-5 y 7-6(5), en 2 horas y 35 minutos. A sus 39 años, la leyenda de Belgrado ya había sufrido mucho para derrotar en el debut al galo Ugo Humbert. Nole se queda a 69 puntos de Jódar, al que no superará esta semana en las listas. De esta forma, sólo Alex de Miñaur y Taylor Fritz pueden evitar que el joven madrileño se estrene entre los 10 mejores el próximo lunes 2 de noviembre. Djokovic es undécimo en la Race 2026, que da uno de los cinco billetes restantes a la cita de maestros. El campeón de 24 grandes está a 294 puntos de Rafa, que ahora mismo sería el último en entrar en el cartel de los titulares. Falta saber el alcance de la lesión de Flavio Cobolli en Viena. La semana que viene se decide todo en el Masters 1000 de París, con una bolsa en juego de 1.000 puntos. Por el mismo lado del cuadro de Basilea sigue avanzando Taylor Fritz, otro de los aspirantes a estar en Turín. Tras acabar con la resistencia de Denis Shapovalov, por 6-4 y 6-3, le espera Arthur Fils. El galo es la séptima raqueta del curso.

articles.title: Born in Russia, championed by Kazakhstan: How the country turned imported tennis talent into homegrown inspiration
articles.summary: At the Almaty Arena, children as young as five waited with their parents to meet Alexander Bublik. He was delayed due to a miscommunication.
articles.body: At the Almaty Arena, children as young as five waited with their parents to meet Alexander Bublik. He was delayed due to a miscommunication. Two hours after the scheduled time, they were still waiting. When Kazakhstan's leading male tennis player finally arrived, he spent 40 minutes signing autographs, staying until every child had his signature on a cap, a ball or a jacket. A decade ago, when Kazakhstan took a chance on the 6-foot-5-inch Bublik, he was ranked around No. 500. Last week, children queued up at a luminous arena for a moment with him. "At the beginning I came here as a guest, as a foreigner," Bublik said, replying to a question from TOI. "I was just a guy who was brought to the team, in a way, and along the way I developed an emotional connection with the people, with the country."That journey from recruit to someone a country cheers as its own is at the heart of Kazakhstan's tennis story. Its leading man, Bublik, and women's world No. 1 Elena Rybakina were both born in Russia. Rybakina became the first player representing Kazakhstan to top the world rankings in Sept. Their beginnings were less grand. For Rybakina's family, the dilemma was one many Indian parents would recognise: pursue an uncertain sporting career or secure an education? In a 2020 interview with the WTA Insider, she recalled having about 15 offers from American universities. Her father wanted her to take that route. Money was tight; an injury could undo everything. "My dad really wanted me to go," she said.Then Kazakhstan offered support, making the decision easier. She switched allegiance in 2018, well before becoming a Grand Slam champion. Rybakina and her parents flew to Kazakhstan to meet federation president Bulat Utemuratov, the businessman behind its tennis boom. The backing helped turn a precarious ambition into a sparkling career. She finished 2018 ranked No. 191; a year later, she was No. 37. Wimbledon followed in 2022, and 2026 brought two more major titles. Bublik, who began playing at age two under his father and childhood coach, Stanislav, joined Kazakhstan in 2016. "I needed support, I needed people who would care about me, and Kazakhstan gave me all that," he said. The strategy paired two ambitions: to give promising players the backing to compete internationally, and to give Kazakhstan's children heroes they could watch and emulate. Recruiting talent offered a quicker route to the first goal while courts, coaching and junior programmes developed at home.According to KTF vice-president Dias Doskarayev, the country had 60 courts 19 years ago in 2007 - the year Utemuratov took over as president of the association - with many of them in disrepair. Today, it has 412. More than 25,000 children play tennis regularly, he says, while the federation fully funds over 1,000 children, including their coaching, equipment and travel. Eva Korysheva, 16, from Aktobe in western Kazakhstan, studies Rybakina's composure as closely as her strokes. "I admire the way she carries herself on court. She stays calm and focused," she said."Elena's serve is her biggest weapon. I would love to have a serve as powerful as hers!" Kazakhstan is not alone in finding sporting success through talent born elsewhere. Qatar naturalised athletes like Saif Saaeed Shaheen and Femi Ogunode, among others. Singapore's China-born Feng Tianwei helped its women beat China to become world team table-tennis champions in 2010. Her route to Singapore began with a sports scholarship.The harder question is what follows the imported success. Kazakhstan's recent results at the junior level offer evidence of progress. Between 2022 and 2026, 17 Kazakhstani players competed in junior Grand Slam tournaments. Significantly, all were born in Kazakhstan. India, once an Asian powerhouse, had just nine players compete in the same period. That is an important distinction for a federation that initially relied on recruiting established players from abroad. Can admiration become participation, and participation produce champions developed at home? Kazakhstan's investment in a grassroots programme and modern infrastructure gives that ambition a spine. For now, the connection is visible: a teenager studying a serve, a player making a junior Grand Slam semifinal, children waiting for an autograph. "I'll do everything I can for the children, the federation and the fans," Bublik said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: La WTA prohíbe a Quevedo lucir un crespón negro por las víctimas del accidente ferroviario de Urda
articles.standfirst: La canaria quería tener un recuerdo por lo sucedido en España como hizo Rafa Jódar en Basilea
articles.summary: La canaria quería tener un recuerdo por lo sucedido en España como hizo Rafa Jódar en Basilea
articles.body: La ATP y la WTA son dos mundos totalmente distintos. Son dos circuitos profesionales, masculino y femenino, en que se juega a tenis, pero las diferencias siguen siendo muchas. Una prueba más de ello se ha dado este viernes en el torneo de Guangzhou (China). Kaitlin Quevedo, consciente de la situación que está atravesando su país tras el accidente ferroviario en Urda que le ha costado la vida a 69 personas, pidió poder jugar con un crespón negro los cuartos de final contra la suiza Jill Teichmann. Las autoridades de la WTA, según ha podido saber MARCA, le contestaron que el negro está prohibido y que el crespón podía ser de cualquier color, pero no negro. De esta forma, Kaitlin, de 20 años y flamante campeona este curso en Sao Paulo, se ha quedado con las ganas de mostrar su luto por lo que está pasando en España. La ATP sí permitió el jueves que Rafa Jódar luciera un crespón negro en su partido de la segunda ronda de Basilea ante Valentin Vacherot. Cabe recordar que la WTA sí permite salir a Naomi Osaka disfrazada a la pista en cada uno de los torneos del Grand Slam.

articles.title: Harriet Dart reaches Guangzhou Open semi-final as Elena Rybakina withdraws with injury at Pan Pacific Open
articles.summary: Great Britain's Harriet Dart reaches semi-finals of Guangzhou Open; world No 1 Elena Rybakina withdraws from tournament in Japan; watch the WTA and ATP Tours live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The British No 3 looked up against it after losing the first set 6-3 but rebounded brilliantly to win the next two sets 6-2 6-4, securing her fifth victory in a row and one of the finest of her career.

"It was an incredible battle," Dart said in her on-court interview on Sky Sports. "I thought Paula started really strongly. I was always behind, but I knew going in that it was going to be an incredibly tough match.

"I really needed to hang in there in the tough moments, and maybe I'd get a chance. Luckily I was able to take my chances today and I'm really excited to be in the semi-final.

"It's been a very long time since I've been in the business end of a (WTA) tournament, so I'm very proud of that."

Dart is into her first WTA semi-final since the Transylvania Open in 2024, having beaten Tatiana Prozorova and Janice Tjen in the earlier stages after coming through two qualifying rounds.

Rybakina withdraws from Pan Pacific Open with injury

World No 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew injured against Leylah Fernandez in the Pan Pacific Open to exit the tournament at the quarter-final stage.

The Kazakh player withdrew from the match before a point was played, giving the Canadian Fernandez safe passage into the last four in Tokyo, where she will play Kamilla Rakhimova for a place in the final.

"I just wanted to say thank you so much for coming today, but unfortunately I won't be able to play," the 27-year-old said on-court.

"I've been struggling for a couple of days with a little injury.

"It's difficult for me to come and play at 100 per cent since there is also a very important tournament coming up."

Rybakina beat Yulia Putintseva 6-2, 6-3 to advance to the quarterfinals and will stay the world No 1 at the conclusion of a year in which she won two Grand Slams - the Australian Open and the U.S. Open.

Having won Wimbledon in 2022, Rybakina - a 27-year-old born in Russia but representing Kazakhstan - is only a French Open title away from completing the career Grand Slam.

She described her year-end status as "an incredibly special moment for me."

"I'm really proud of what I've achieved this season and the consistency I've shown throughout the year," said Rybakina, who also won titles in Stuttgart and Ningbo and rose to No. 1 in the world for the first time by winning the U.S. Open.

Rybakina will be honoured with a trophy to mark the achievement during a special presentation at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells from November 8-15.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic's ATP Finals blow with Jan-Lennard Struff defeat
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic's hopes of reaching the ATP Finals in Turin next month fade with a surprise defeat by Jan-Lennard Struff in Basel.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic's hopes of making a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals have been dented by a surprise defeat against Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel.

Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) - the first time he has been beaten by Struff in nine meetings.

"I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So, I was very, very happy," said the world number 27.

"I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. The last eight times he beat me very, very easily. So, I'm very, very happy and pleased with the performance."

The year's top-eight performers qualify for the ATP event in Turin and this result leaves Djokovic - the men's game's record 24-time Grand Slam winner - 11th in the standings.

Djokovic admitted he expected to feel "a little rusty" after his win against Frenchman Ugo Humbert on Wednesday, but now faces a fight to make the finals as he is outside the top 10 for the first time since 2018.

Zverev seals world number one spot at earliest opportunity

Rafael Jodar holds the final qualifying spot in ninth place, because number one Jannik Sinner is injured and will not take part.

Djokovic is 319 points behind Jodar, although he has the opportunity at the Paris Masters in November to move up the rankings.

The Serb is aiming to move ahead of Roger Federer with his 19th appearance at the finals in Turin.

He has won the event a record seven times and has missed the past two editions with injury - but the last time he failed to qualify on merit was in 2017, when his season was affected by injury.

Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have their places confirmed for the showpiece event in Italy from 15-22 November, although American Shelton also surprisingly lost in Basel.

The top seed lost 6-3 6-7 (4-7) 7-6 (7-1) to Swiss wildcard Jerome Kym, who is ranked 222nd in the world.

articles.title: El supuesto triángulo amoroso que revoluciona el tenis: "¿Si le he sido infiel a Berrettini? Lávate la boca"
articles.standfirst: La bailarina Vanessa Bellini ha roto su silencio para responder a los rumores sobre su supuesta infidelidad a Matteo Berrettini con su amigo Lorenzo Musetti
articles.summary: La bailarina Vanessa Bellini ha roto su silencio para responder a los rumores sobre su supuesta infidelidad a Matteo Berrettini con su amigo Lorenzo Musetti
articles.body: Vanessa Bellini, la expareja del tenista Matteo Berrettini, ha roto su silencio sobre lo que en Italia han bautizado como "caso Berrettini". Tras los rumores de una supuesta infidelidad que pudo haber significado su distanciamiento tras un año de relación, la bailarina respondió directamente en Instagram a un comentario: "Tolero todas las tonterías que dicen y escriben, y simplemente lo dejo pasar (leo mucho, pero he aprendido que así es como funciona el mundo). ¿Pero decir que yo habría traicionado a Matteo? ¡Por favor! Lávate la boca antes de hablar". Esta semana han circulado diversas especulaciones sugiriendo que Vanessa Bellini habría mantenido un romance con Lorenzo Musetti, tenista y amigo íntimo de Berrettini. Matteo Berrettini, finalista de Wimbledon en 2021, ha dejado de seguir a Lorenzo Musetti en Instagram recientemente. Los rumores cobraron fuerza cuando, durante el torneo de Viena le preguntaron a Berrettini si el reciente título de Musetti en Lyon le servía de "inspiración". Berrettini no respondió de inmediato y, tras preguntar "¿está esto en directo?", ofreció entre unas risas incómodas una respuesta que pareció bastante comedida: "Está bien. Sé que se esforzó mucho por regresar y supongo que se lo merecía". Por su parte Musetti, que sale con Veronica Confalonieri desde 2022, no se ha pronunciado públicamente sobre los rumores.

articles.title: Guangzhou Open: Harriet Dart reaches second WTA Tour semi-final of career
articles.summary: Harriet Dart reaches the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career as she fights back from a set down to beat Paula Badosa in the Guangzhou Open.
articles.body:
Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career when she fought back from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa at the Guangzhou Open in China.

The 30-year-old triumphed 3-6 6-2 6-4 against Spain's Badosa - ranked 54 places above her - in two hours and 15 minutes at Nansha International Tennis Centre.

Dart's first appearance in the semi-finals of a tour event was in the Transylvania Open in Cluj-Napoca, where she lost in straight sets to Karolina Pliskova.

She will face 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in the last four on Saturday.

"It's been a very long time since I've been in the business end of the tournament so I am really excited for that," Dart said.

"Tennis is so stressful, so to have the opportunity to compete again on Saturday is a great opportunity for me."

Dart, who came through qualifying and beat second-seed Janice Tjen in the previous round, lost her opening service game in the first set but broke back and drew level at 3-3.

However, former world number two Badosa broke Dart's serve again to take a 5-3 lead and held her serve to close out the set.

The pair exchanged breaks at the start of the second set before Dart seized the upper hand to level at 1-1.

Badosa, who required two medical timeouts during the match as she appeared to struggle with the heat, saved a match point at 5-3 in the deciding set and then broke Dart's serve.

But the Spaniard, ranked 61st in the world, was running on empty in her next service game, as Dart won it to love.

"It was an incredible battle. I thought Paula started really strongly. I was always behind, and knew it was going to be an incredibly tough match," Dart added.

"I really needed to hang in there during the tough moments and wait for a chance. Luckily I was able to take my chance, and I am very excited to be in the semi-finals."

Analysis: How Wimbledon champion is helping Dart flourish

Dart reached a career high of 70th in the world in 2024, having made the Wimbledon third round and US Open second round, but has been languishing outside the top 100 for the vast majority of the past two seasons.

The run from Guangzhou qualifying to the last four puts her on the cusp of the top 100 once again, meaning she has a good chance of going straight into the main draw of the Australian Open in January without needing to qualify.

That would be rich reward for a superb second half to the season, where she has struck the ball consistently well and continued to grow in confidence.

Working with former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli has been a big factor in Dart's resurgence.

The pair live close to each other and began working together earlier this year. Dart has enjoyed soaking up the knowledge and experience imparted by the French former world number seven in their ad hoc coaching partnership.

Dart says she has also benefitted from Bartoli still "hitting a good ball" in practice.

The arrangement has helped Dart win 17 of her 22 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon, taking her overall record on the WTA Tour this season to 21 victories from 32 matches - the highest winning percentage of her career.

articles.title: Kaitlin Quevedo avanza a semifinales y Paula Badosa cae en el WTA 250 de Cantón
articles.standfirst: La primera venció a la suiza Jil Teichmann mientras que Paula perdió ante la británica Harriet Dart en tres sets
articles.summary: Pierde ante la británica Harriet Dart en tres sets
articles.body: Kaitlin Quevedo avanzó a las semifinales de final del WTA 250 de Cantón (China) tras vencer a la suiza Jil Teichmann por 7-6, 6-3, mientras que Paula Badosa cayó en su duelo de cuartos ante la británica Harriet Dart en tres sets (6-3, 2-6 y 4-6). Quevedo, 86 del mundo, se enfrentó por primera vez a la helvética, con la que disputó un ajustado primer set en el que la española de 20 años, tras lograr una ventaja de 4-1, vio como Teichmann igualaba el tanteo. Una tónica que se repitió durante todo el primer parcial hasta que Quevedo se impuso 7-2 en el tie break. Las tornas cambiaron en el segundo, en el que Teichmann comenzó con ventaja de 0-2, pero una Kaitlin lanzada logró un contrabreak de inmediato y cerró el partido con su quinta rotura de servicio a la suiza en su cuarta pelota de partido. Quevedo, que buscará su segundo título de la WTA tras su victoria en San Paulo el pasado mes de septiembre, espera rival en la semifinal, que saldrá de la vencedora entre Lilli Tagger y Han Shi, aún por disputarse a lo largo de la jornada de hoy. En cuanto a Badosa, 61 en el ranking de la WTA, se impuso en el primer set, pero se vio superada en los dos siguientes por la londinense, 115 en la clasificación mundial. La española había superado en octavos a la austriaca Sinja Kraus por 6-1 y 6-4. Badosa afrontaba este torneo de pista dura siendo la quinta cabeza de serie y después de haber caído en primera ronda durante su participación previa en Osaka (Japón).

articles.title: Novak Djokovic: After shock defeat in Basel former world No 1 heads to Paris Masters in race to make ATP Finals in Turin
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic needs at the very least a semi-final at the Paris Masters to have a chance to make the ATP Finals in Turin; a final would likely do it, and a title would surely do it; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday November 2
articles.body:
Defeat has left the Serb with precious few opportunities to make up ground in the race to Turin.

Back ‌in Basel for the first time in 15 years, 39-year-old Djokovic fell 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (5-7) in the second round, his first defeat by German veteran Struff in nine meetings.

The result left Djokovic 11th in the qualification race for the eight-player season finale, ​319 points behind ninth-placed Rafael Jodar, who currently occupies the final qualifying spot with ⁠Jannik Sinner not playing in Turin due to injury.

A total of five main-draw spots now remain, with as many as 10 players still in contention.

Alexander ⁠Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton all have places in the ATP Finals starting on November 15, leaving Djokovic battling for one of the remaining spots ‌with next week's Paris Masters offering him another opportunity to pick up points.

It seems likely that Daniil Medvedev and Arthur Fils will claim two of the five remaining spots. This would leave three places available for a group of eight players: Djokovic, Jodar, Flavio Cobolli, Frances Tiafoe, Alex de Minaur, Taylor Fritz, Tommy Paul and Jakub Mensik.

However, Cobolli suffered an injury during his match against Matteo Berrettini in Vienna, leaving him visibly emotional and in tears on court, leaving a big question mark about whether he will be able to compete for the remainder of the season.

There are five players currently separated by fewer than 500 points, with Djokovic firmly in the middle of that group.

He will head to the French capital as a record seven-time champion but would likely need at least a semi-final appearance alongside early exits for some of the players around him in the rankings to put himself in a position to qualify.

Djokovic may even consider ‌entering the ATP 250 event in Stockholm afterwards if he still needs points to secure a spot in Turin.

He missed the previous two editions of the ATP Finals due to injury but had indicated that he intended to return to the event aiming to claim a record-extending eighth title.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion ⁠has endured another tough season physically, though his run to the Australian Open final, ​a Wimbledon semi-final and his Beijing triumph have provided notable highs.

Few will ​write off Djokovic's chances of reaching Turin even at this stage, given the resilience that ​he has shown throughout his glittering career.

"I won the title in Beijing a few weeks ago, ⁠which was definitely my best week this year apart from the Grand Slam final in Australia," Djokovic said in Basel.

"It's been a year with a lot of struggles, particularly physically, but I'm still here ⁠and as competitive as anybody. If somebody beats me, well ​done, good job, but I'm definitely going to fight and not give these youngsters too easy ​a stroll on court. They have to earn their victories.

"That's also what motivates me: seeing how I can match up with players 15-plus years younger than me. ‌It's been quite an interesting process ​to experience."

Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from November 2.

articles.title: Sania Mirza, Mahesh Bhupathi's nominations ratified for AITA elections
articles.summary: New Delhi: The All India Tennis Association (AITA) has ratified all five nominations for the Sports Person of Outstanding Merit (SOM) Executive Committee,
articles.body: New Delhi: The All India Tennis Association (AITA) has ratified all five nominations for the Sports Person of Outstanding Merit (SOM) Executive Committee, while the eight candidates who had originally filed nominations for the SOM General Body have also been declared valid, setting the stage for the next phase of the federation's electoral process.The five candidates whose nominations for the Executive Committee have been found valid are Ankita Bhambri, Janaki Krishnamoorthy, Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza and Vishal Uppal.The list for the SOM General Body features eight names: Ankita Bhambri, Ashutosh Singh, Gaurav Natekar, Janaki Krishnamoorthy, Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza, Shalini Thakur Chawla and Vishal Uppal.The ratification means all eight candidates who had filed nominations for the General Body have cleared the scrutiny process. The five candidates for the Executive Committee are also through, with the two lists sharing the same five names.Bhupathi and Sania, two of India's most accomplished tennis players, have filed nominations for both positions. The other three candidates in the Executive Committee race are former players Ankita Bhambri, Janaki Krishnamoorthy and current Billie Jean King Cup captain Vishal Uppal.The development follows the nomination process for the November 7 SOM elections, which has attracted considerable attention after former India tennis star Leander Paes did not file his nomination.Paes, the only player in Tier I of the 40-member SOM roster, was seen as a potential candidate for the AITA presidency after the Bengal Tennis Association (BTA), headed by him, publicly backed his candidature.However, his absence from the SOM nominations has effectively ruled out that route to the presidency. Under the amended AITA Constitution, Paes remains ineligible to contest as a state representative as he has not completed at least one term as an office-bearer in a state association. While he can participate in the November 27 AITA elections as Bengal's representative, he cannot contest for a position in the national body through that route.The amended AITA Constitution provides for four SOM representatives in the General Body, comprising two men and two women, and two representatives in the 15-member Executive Committee, with one position each reserved for a man and a woman.The SOM framework is part of the broader effort to ensure greater representation of accomplished sportspersons in the governance of national sports federations under the new sports governance rules.Bhupathi, a former world No. 1 in doubles and multiple Grand Slam champion, had earlier underlined the importance of having elite athletes involved in sports administration.With the nominations now ratified, the focus shifts to the SOM electoral process ahead of the AITA's November 27 elections.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: World number one Rybakina withdraws from Pan Pacific Open with neck injury
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina expects to return for next month’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells after withdrawing from the Tokyo quarterfinals.
articles.body:
Elena Rybakina has pulled out of the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo with a neck injury, a day after she secured the year-end world number one ranking.

The Moscow-born Kazakh was due to face Canada’s Leylah Fernandez in the quarterfinals, but instead she came onto the court to address the crowd and sign autographs.

She said she would return for next month’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

“I just wanted to say thank you so much for coming today, but unfortunately I won’t be able to play,” said the 27-year-old.

“I’ve been struggling for a couple of days with a little injury. It’s difficult for me to come and play at 100 percent since there is also a very important tournament coming up.”

Rybakina clinched the year-end top ranking with a 6-2, 6-3 win over Yulia Putintseva in her opening match in Tokyo.

She became world number one for the first time last month after winning the US Open , replacing Aryna Sabalenka at the summit.

The achievement capped a year in which Rybakina also won the Australian Open in January and now has three Grand Slam titles.

She arrived in Tokyo after winning her fourth title of the season last week at the Ningbo Open in China, beating Fernandez in the final.

“Thank you so much for all the support throughout the year, especially here in Tokyo,” she said.

“It’s an amazing city. I really enjoy it every time I come. Thanks again and hope to see you all next year.”
